operation: Q6 elliptic projection / CG on cell and face fields
probable_cost: high when projectionEnable=true; historical profiling identified q6_projection as dominant after cleanup
parallelism: high: regular cell/face arrays, stencil operator, vector AXPY, dot reductions
memory_difficulty: moderate: iterative global reductions and persistent device arrays, but no particle scatter
numerical_risk: moderate: floating-point reduction order may alter residual trajectory; compare tolerances not bitwise identity
cpu_gpu_comparison: very good: divergence residuals, CG iterations, velocity correction, mass/momentum summaries
physical_interest: very high for TG, Poiseuille, obstacle/step, piston whenever Q6 is active
notes: Start with a grid-only backend for the elliptic CG path; keep CPU OpenMP as default reference.

operation: Particle-to-cell deposits for collision, Q6, thermostat, resampling, capacity
probable_cost: high and repeated; resampling may call full deposits several times per step
parallelism: high over particles, then over cells
memory_difficulty: high: scatter/reduction to cells; CPU currently avoids atomics through per-thread local arrays
numerical_risk: moderate to high: reduction order and cell-id conventions affect downstream Q6/resampling
cpu_gpu_comparison: good but requires invariant checks on mass, momentum, population and per-cell diagnostics
physical_interest: very high for all validation cases, especially resampling and piston/capacity
first_gpu_priority: second target after grid-only Q6, or first target only for a CPU/device-resident architecture
notes: A GPU implementation should choose between atomics, sort/bin-by-cell, or two-level block reductions.

operation: SRC collision update by particle after cell moments
probable_cost: medium to high; one main particle pass plus wall virtual-particle cell pass
parallelism: high once cell moments are known
memory_difficulty: moderate: cell moment arrays are read-only during velocity rotation; deposit remains the hard part
numerical_risk: low to moderate: random rotation sign must remain deterministic; wallVP random thermal noise must be controlled
cpu_gpu_comparison: good: kBT, momentum, wallVP counters, velocity statistics
physical_interest: high for every case; wallVP makes Poiseuille/piston sensitive
first_gpu_priority: good follow-up if deposits are also on device
notes: The rotation pass itself is GPU-friendly, but moving only this pass would be transfer dominated.

probable_cost: medium; active in validated thermal wall/channel cases
parallelism: high but multi-pass: moments, kinetic, scales, particle rescale
memory_difficulty: moderate to high: same scatter/reduction pattern as collision plus extra kinetic reduction
numerical_risk: moderate: thermostat affects kBT and viscosity; reduction order affects scales weakly
cpu_gpu_comparison: very good: kBTBefore/kBTAfter, scale extrema, particlesRescaled
physical_interest: high for Poiseuille, piston, wallVP; lower for pure TG if thermostat disabled
first_gpu_priority: not first unless deposit infrastructure exists
notes: Useful once collision/deposit arrays are device-resident; otherwise CPU/GPU transfer overhead dominates.

operation: Weighted resampling, population guard, remap, thermal renormalization, mass guard
probable_cost: high in Q6+resampling; repeated deposits and role mutations can dominate
parallelism: mixed: deposits are parallel; candidate lists, pool edits, transfer plans are irregular
memory_difficulty: very high: dynamic lists, particle role changes, pool free slots, conservative remap
numerical_risk: high: this is physically delicate and protects poor cells; trajectory equality is fragile
cpu_gpu_comparison: moderate: many diagnostics exist, but exact CPU/GPU path equivalence is difficult
physical_interest: very high physically, but too risky for first GPU kernel
notes: Keep on CPU until the field/deposit backbone is stable on GPU.

probable_cost: low to medium except piston/capacity studies
memory_difficulty: moderate: deposit mass plus grid gradient and particle velocity update
numerical_risk: moderate to high in piston/capacity because pressure response is physically central
cpu_gpu_comparison: good: virial pressure, wall loads, momentum correction residuals
physical_interest: high for piston only; secondary for TG/Poiseuille/obstacle
notes: Good GPU candidate once cell mass deposit and particle update infrastructure is already available.

probable_cost: low in light mode; diagnostics are not the target bottleneck
parallelism: high reductions, but summary cadence is sparse
numerical_risk: low, but diagnostics must remain CPU-visible
cpu_gpu_comparison: excellent, but not worth first acceleration
physical_interest: diagnostic value high; acceleration value low
notes: Preserve as validation oracle; do not offload first.
